title: Symbiotic Task Scheduling and Data Prefetching
problem: Hardware task-parallel systems that operate with fine-grained tasks (approx. 100-cycle execution time) cannot benefit from conventional hardware prefetchers because tasks are too short for prefetches to complete before the task finishes, leaving DRAM latency fully exposed and undermining the performance gains of hardware task management.
motivation: Many-core hardware task-parallel systems (hundreds of cores) already accelerate irregular workloads 3-60x over software, but DRAM latency exposure due to short tasks is the remaining bottleneck, and no existing prefetching scheme is aware of task-function data-access patterns or the upcoming task schedule.
method: The Task-Seeded Prefetcher (TSP) learns the data-access pattern of each task function type and issues prefetches as soon as a task descriptor is queued by the hardware task scheduler, using the descriptor as a seed to identify which memory addresses the task will access. The Memory Response Task Scheduler (MRS) augments the baseline task-to-core dispatch policy by monitoring prefetch completion status from TSP: when a task's prefetches are done, MRS preferentially dispatches it to a ready core, maximizing prefetch utilization without stalling the pipeline. Together, TSP and MRS form a symbiotic pair where scheduling drives prefetching and prefetch status informs scheduling.
key_novelty: A symbiotic co-design of a function-aware task-seeded prefetcher (TSP) and a prefetch-status-aware task scheduler (MRS) that together exploit the task descriptor queue as an early prefetch trigger in hardware task-parallel systems.
contributions: Task-Seeded Prefetcher (TSP): learns and prefetches per-task-function data-access patterns, seeded from task descriptors queued before dispatch
Memory Response Task Scheduler (MRS): uses TSP prefetch status to optimize core dispatch decisions and improve prefetch hit rates
Speedups of up to 3.1x (geometric mean up to 1.4x) across 13 benchmarks on 256-core task-parallel systems
Demonstrated additive benefit on systems already 3-60x faster than parallel software

metrics.speedup: up to 3.1x; geometric mean up to 1.4x across 13 benchmarks on 256-core systems

primary_theme: symbiotic task-seeded prefetching and scheduling for hardware task-parallel systems
